source_text.gate: TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR gate for REQ-519 slice 2f-a (GH #2535), uncommitted tree on feature/WF02-REQ519-2FA-GATE-20261019. Mix ran per file set, one mix at a time, under the shared mixlock directory (taken with mkdir, released by the creating script; other sessions' locks (letflow-3) were waited for, never removed). No full suite, no letflow.check.test. Mutants compiled in memory only.

task.description: Hard gate on TEST-DESIGNER 2f-a tests: REQ-519 ACs 7 (2f-a part), 8-15 as assigned to 2f-a, every SEC step-16 merge condition, REVIEWER step-17 notes; the deferred (dormant) items; isolation, formatting, log lesson, flake and CI-environment risk; own mutants.

result.summary: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS. No coverage gap in what 2f-a can show. EXECUTED (MIX_ENV=test, one mix at a time under the mixlock): after mix compile --force (504 files, exit 0, no warning) eight in-memory mutants V1..V8 (7 killed, 1 survives by construction, see below); after my two test-support edits the seven new files together, seed 4242, LOG_LEVEL=error: Result: 133 passed in 127.8 s, 0 compiler warnings; the three neighbours (sync_scope_guard_test, scope_enforcement_test, routers/tenant_scope_enforcement_test): Result: 89 passed in 84.7 s; mix format --check-formatted (the real mix task, calibrated: it rejects a deliberately unformatted file) exit 0 on the fixture, all seven new test files and the two edited neighbours, before and after my edit. Of the items the designer lists as not testable while `on` is dormant, NONE can be tested durably without touching lib/: every one lives in a PRIVATE function on the shadow -> on path of flip/4 (do_flip, on_checks!, record_refusal, flush_before?, clock/1 only used for target on) that check_target/1 shields; the only seams would be recompiling ScopeEnforcement with a widened @modes inside the test VM (global module replacement, unsafe for later tests) or a lib change. The spec carries every one of them as an explicit 2f-b obligation (table 'What 2f-a cannot show'), nothing is silently dropped; I add one machine-readable list below (obligations_for_2f_b) for the next step to copy.

changes_made.change: with_plain_schema/2 and with_renamed_table!/3 now ALSO register an idempotent on_exit restore (restore_schema/2 checks pg_namespace first; restore_table/3 uses ALTER TABLE IF EXISTS); added import ExUnit.Callbacks, only: [on_exit: 1]. The existing `after` restores stay.
changes_made.why: ExUnit kills the test process on a timeout (Process.exit :kill), which skips an `after`. For a renamed TABLE the leak was harmless (the tenant teardown DROPs the schema CASCADE), but a killed with_plain_schema/2 would leave a schema named req519_plain_N behind that the teardown (which drops by the ORIGINAL name) never removes. on_exit runs after a kill and, being registered later than the tenant fixture's own on_exit, runs BEFORE its teardown (LIFO).
changes_made.verified: mix format --check-formatted exit 0; the seven files re-ran: 133 passed, 0 warnings, LOG_LEVEL=error

changes_made.change: renamed the test 'each table a fact reads, renamed inside a rolled-back transaction, makes evaluate/3 RAISE' to '... renamed with committed DDL, ...'
changes_made.why: the title described the first form of the test that the designer had to abandon (MU-28 survived it); the body and the spec say committed DDL. A stale title misleads the next reader into re-introducing the weak form.

findings.title: Restoration of committed DDL was not robust to a killed test process (fixed by this validator)
findings.detail: See changes_made. Test failures (assertion or raise) were already safe: the `after` ran. Only a kill (timeout) was exposed, and only for with_plain_schema/2 was the leak real (an orphan schema in the partition database; no other test enumerates it, because its name is not tenant_%).

findings.title: V7 survives by construction: attrs[:now] honoured when not a DateTime
findings.detail: clock/1 runs for every target but its value is consumed only on the on path, which parse_mode/check_target shield. Mutant V7 (`_other -> DateTime.utc_now()` replaced by `other -> other`) passes dormant_on_test, as the designer predicted. The guard is pinned only through its observable halves (junk never crashes a shadow flip, the router builds a literal 3-key map, the body cannot carry a clock). The clause itself is a 2f-b obligation.
findings.required_action: 2f-b: with `on` settable, assert flip/4 with a non-DateTime attrs[:now] uses the server clock (junk 'now' strings must not widen or shorten the window); kill V7.

findings.title: The flip-level dormant path has NO test at all until 2f-b
findings.detail: do_flip/on_checks!/record_refusal/flush_before? for target on, the S lock before the six facts, the gate raise inside the flip being a 500, the refusal audit after the rollback and shadow_required from off are all unexercised (they are unreachable from any route; SEC accepted that). The module-level pieces they call (OnGate, RefusedAudit.record/6, ShadowWindow.flush_evidence/0, ScopeEnforcement.integrity/1) are all covered and mutation-measured. A defect in the glue (e.g. wrong previous-mode argument, missing flush) is invisible until 2f-b adds tests; 2f-b must NOT merge without them.

findings.title: Held-lock tests use the shared 700 ms per-phase deadline
findings.detail: T-G10c uses Letflow.LockOrderHelpers.wait_for_blocked/2 (as T-S15 in 2e-b). A badly overloaded host can only produce a false failure, never a false pass. The lock holder is released in on_exit and its own receive is bounded at 15 s.

findings.title: Wall-clock use is flake-safe at UTC midnight
findings.detail: Every day-count test derives its window from fx.now = t0 + 7 days (t0 is the real flip entry's timestamp), so the window moves with t0, not with the clock at assertion time. The three tests that use the real clock do not depend on the date: satisfy!/eval share one DateTime (T-E1d); T-E16 passes the date explicitly to record/counts_by_day; the integrity router test redoes its seed when Date.utc_today() changed (bounded, 3 tries). Whole-second duration boundaries use t0 +/- n s so the fractional part cancels.

fixture_and_flake_review.isolation: All seven new files are async: false and build their own committed tenants through OnGateFixture (admin_tenant!/shadow_tenant! over TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!, on_exit teardown that DROPs the schema CASCADE). No test depends on another: each builds its own tenant; no shared hardcoded state beyond slug prefixes unique per test. Fault triggers are dropped in `after`. Committed DDL (table/schema renames) is now restored in `after` AND `on_exit` (F-1). VM-global application env is restored by with_env/3 in an `after`. No hardcoded secret or connection string.
fixture_and_flake_review.formatting: mix format --check-formatted (the real task, not Code.format_string!) exit 0 on the fixture, the seven new test files and both edited neighbours; the check was proven live on a deliberately unformatted file.
fixture_and_flake_review.log_lesson: Refutations on ids are made only on the module's own constant lines (F.lines_with(log, marker)) or on payload dumps, never over a whole capture that contains Ecto debug QUERY lines. The 'gate logs nothing' test filters on the substring scope_enforcement and separately refutes lf_tok_ only.
fixture_and_flake_review.flake: see F-5 and F-4. No Process.sleep in the new files; queue order via pg_locks helper; no per-entity INSERT list compared.
fixture_and_flake_review.ci_environment: mix compile --force before the baseline (no stale _build dependence); LOG_LEVEL=error run: 133 passed (the log assertions use Logger.error lines, so no level dependence); config/test.exs sets only the pre-existing :scope_shadow_flush_interval_ms (1 h) which T-E16 relies on and asserts first; runtime 127.8 s for the seven files on this host (tenant provisioning dominates); ShadowEvidence ETS counters are VM-global but the tests use their own schema names and an explicit flush, and flush failures for dropped schemas are rescued.
